newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nearby Bremen cotton prices rise on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Nearby Bremen cotton prices rise on tight supply.

text.p: European cotton consumers are faced with higher spot prices as African and Asian old crop supplies are thinning, the Bremen Cotton Exchange said in a market report.
Demand for strict-lowmiddling qualities was especially not matched by adequate origin supplies so that buyers turned to the trade for second hand offers.
The Exchange reported sales of Central Asian standards 1, 2 and 3 as well as West African supply and East African Acala for June/July through December 1997.

Other trades included Argentine medium grades for the third quarter, U.S. cotton (MOT) for June/July only, Syrian medium/high grades for the second half of 1997 and Chad cotton for all dates through third quarter 1998.
In extra longstapes, the Exchange reported activity in Israel-Pima for second and third quarter 1997 as well as U.S.-Pkma for fourth quarter 1997/first quarter 1998.
Cotton stocks as of May 29 totalled 38,018 bales, down from 126,250 bales a year earlier and compared with 36,007 bales a fortnight earlier.
